title: lwb Proof of Completion record
description: Owner directive 7: Proof of Completion on every deliverable; done = committed AND pushed with a proof record and green CI. See proof/README.md.

deliverable.description: The deliverable's id, e.g. an issue/step number or a short slug.

pr.description: The PR number this record proves. Optional in the schema, but it is the ONLY thing the directive-7 gates key on, both pre-merge (lwb-proof-pr) and post-merge (lwb-proof-coverage) -- the squash-merge commit does not exist while a PR's own CI runs, so 'commit' cannot be matched pre-merge. Do NOT reintroduce a fallback onto 'deliverable': a deliverable is documented below as an issue/step number or a slug, so a small integer there is ordinary usage, and accepting it as a PR alias let a record for step 6 of an unrelated plan silently satisfy PR #6's gate. See scripts/lwb_check_proof.py::check_pr_has_record.

author.description: Identity of whoever did the work (a session/dispatch id, not just 'claude' or 'codex').

checked_by.description: Identity of whoever independently checked it. Must differ from 'author' — see the schema-level check in scripts/lwb_check_proof.py.

commit.description: The commit SHA this proof record proves.

argv.description: The exact command run, as an argv list (no shell string — avoids a shell-quoting ambiguity in the proof record itself).

expect_exit.description: The exit code this command was expected to produce.

tail.description: At most the last 10 lines of the command's combined output.

sha256.description: sha256 of the command's full captured output (stdout+stderr concatenated), so a 10-line tail can't quietly hide a truncated failure — see scripts/lwb_check_proof.py's re-hash check.

mutations.description: Every file this deliverable's work created or changed, repo-relative path.

unproven.description: Anything claimed as part of this deliverable that this record does NOT prove (an honest gap list, not a place to hide a failure as a footnote).

acceptance_criteria.description: What 'done' meant for this deliverable, agreed before the work started; quality floor item 1. Each entry is a criterion and whether it was met -- required, and enforced, for records from PR #12 onward; see scripts/lwb_check_proof.py.

tokens.description: Measured token cost, per the mission's efficiency section: total input, cached input, uncached input, output, retries, setup overhead, tool overhead and wall time, separately, plus where the numbers came from. A field that cannot be measured is recorded as the string "unknown", NEVER as zero -- an unmeasured field recorded as zero is exactly how an efficiency claim gets manufactured. Instruction-length proxies are not billed tokens. Required, and enforced, for records from PR #12 onward; see scripts/lwb_check_proof.py.
